subject: Call recap: concurrency & streaming requirements + regional routing / data residency
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: James Liu <james.liu@acmehealth.com>, ops-plat@acmehealth.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T16:10:00Z
Subject: Call recap: concurrency & streaming requirements + regional routing / data residency

Thanks again for the demo today — great conversation. Quick recap and a few asks so we can align engineering and pricing: 

Key inputs from your side:
- Peak concurrent requests: ~600 RPS during business hours (US east). Typical baseline: 180–220 RPS.
- Average prompt length: 350 tokens; average completion: 220 tokens.
- Streaming: client expects partial token streaming with client-side assembly; low-latency first-token is important (p99 target).
- APAC usage: ~5–8% of traffic initially, EU: 18–22%. EU traffic must not leave EU for PHI-containing requests.

Target SLOs you requested for qualification:
- P50 latency for first token: < 60ms (US), < 80ms (EU), < 140ms (APAC)
- P95 end-to-end generation: < 200ms (US), < 260ms (EU), < 400ms (APAC)
- Availability: 99.9% for serving endpoints; burst capacity support during open hours

Asks / next steps from Redwood:
1) Can you confirm the percent of requests that will use streaming vs non-streaming? (rough split: streaming: ~75%?)
2) Confirm payload variability — percentage of long prompts (>800 tokens) we should expect.
3) Any retention constraints beyond EU-only for PHI (e.g., APAC region-specific restrictions)?
4) We'll attach a draft perf matrix and network diagram for you to annotate.

Attachments: acme_perf_matrix.xlsx (draft throughput/latency table), network_topology_diagram.png

Planned follow-up: propose a technical sync next Tue to validate routing split and pin initial Dedicated capacity for EU + US.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
From: James Liu <james.liu@acmehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-plat@acmehealth.com
Date: 2027-05-02T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Call recap: concurrency & streaming requirements + regional routing / data residency

Appreciate the thorough recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Streaming split: yes — about 70–80% of queries will be streaming (real-time triage UI). The remainder are batched analytics calls.
- Long prompts: very rare — <2% right now. Most prompts are user-facing short contexts (200–600 tokens).
- EU residency: PHI requests must remain in EU and be processed in a customer-controlled VPC if possible. For non-PHI telemetry we can accept cross-region telemetry aggregation.

On SLOs: our product team is comfortable with the p50/p95 ranges you listed for the US and EU. APAC targets are aspirational but the latency differential is acceptable initially.

We need Redwood to confirm whether you recommend Dedicated pools for EU right away or if routing + pinning to EU-hosted hosted nodes would suffice for an initial deployment. Also please surface any minimum committed capacity if we go Dedicated.

FWIW procurement will need an overview of data paths for SOC2 and a short statement on encryption-at-rest and in-transit. Happy to ingest a short doc you can share.

—James
James Liu
Platform Engineering Lead, Acme Health
james.liu@acmehealth.com
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: James Liu <james.liu@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T11:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Call recap: concurrency & streaming requirements + regional routing / data residency

Looping in a couple notes from infra/serving POV — copying James so he has visibility.

Quick feasibility notes: 
- For the bandwidth/latency profile described, we recommend Dedicated for the EU tenant if PHI cannot leave EU. That gives predictable KV cache locality and avoids cross-region egress variability.
- For US traffic a Hosted pool with smart routing + pinned model variant should be OK initially; we can offer a reserve burst bucket to reduce cold-start risk.
- Streaming: our runtime supports continuous streaming with partial-token flush. The critical lever will be batch size controls and per-connection concurrency limits to protect p99 first-token.

Questions for James: 
- Can you send a short sample of your traffic distribution by hour (CSV is fine) so we can run a quick cost/latency projection?
- Do you expect sustained long-running generations (>10s) or mostly sub-2s responses?

Next steps I propose: 
1) Rishi to prepare two options: (A) Hosted + pinned US + Dedicated EU (cost + perf matrix), (B) Dedicated US + EU (commit + pricing).
2) Engineering sync Wed (we can do 45m) to go over perf assumptions and routing mechanics.
3) Short SOC2 & data-path note for procurement — Rishi to draft.

On quoting: if we recommend Dedicated EU we will propose a minimum monthly GPU commitment (we should be explicit about concurrency headroom).

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Product Ops, Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.com

- Streaming: 70–80% of traffic.
- Long prompts: <2%.
- EU PHI: must remain in EU and preferably inside VPC (customer-managed if required).
- Peak concurrency: ~600 RPS (US), baseline 200 RPS.

Redwood next actions (owners & target dates):
- Rishi: deliver Option A & B perf + pricing matrix (attached) by Thu 2027-05-06. (attachment: acme_perf_matrix.xlsx)
- Karthik: engineering feasibility note on Dedicated sizing and minimum commit; initial ballpark by Fri 2027-05-07.
- Evelyn: draft a short SOC2/data-path summary for procurement by Fri 2027-05-07.
- James: share hourly traffic CSV and any specific compliance checklists you want included (expected by Mon 2027-05-10).

Proposed follow-up: schedule a 45m technical sync on 2027-05-11 10:00 AM ET. Rishi will send calendar invite pending your confirmation.

If that all looks right I'll ship the attachments as a follow-up and include a short one-page data-path note.

—Rishi
